headline: New Yorkers will soon need to verify their age to access algorithmic feeds
summary: New York's SAFE for Kids Act, signed in June 2024, mandates age verification for algorithmic social media feeds and late-night notifications, effective January 25, 2027. Non-compliance could lead to fines of up to $5,000 per violation.
details: New Yorkers will soon be required to verify their age to access algorithmic social media feeds or receive notifications between midnight and 6 AM. This applies to platforms with user-generated content where users spend at least 20 percent of their time on algorithmic feeds.

New York Attorney General Letitia James finalized rules for the SAFE for Kids Act, signed into law by Governor Kathy Hochul in June 2024. The law officially takes effect on January 25, 2027, with non-compliant platforms facing penalties up to $5,000 per violation.

Platforms must confirm users' ages with high accuracy, detecting circumvention attempts 98 percent of the time. While government-issued IDs are an option, at least one alternative method must be provided. Age verification data must be immediately deleted or de-identified after use.

For minors, parental consent is required for age-gated features, but platforms cannot block access to non-age-gated parts of the app if consent isn't given. Both parents and children can withdraw consent, and platforms are not obligated to share kids' search history with parents.

The final rules are similar to the initial proposal, but opponents may challenge them in court, citing privacy and speech concerns. Past legal battles have often sided with the tech industry against age verification, though a recent Supreme Court ruling on adult websites may shift the landscape.

headline_marked: [[Claude AI discovers new cryptographic weaknesses]] in HAWK and round-reduced AES
headline: Claude AI discovers new cryptographic weaknesses in HAWK and round-reduced AES
summary: Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview identified improved attacks on HAWK, a post-quantum signature candidate, and a round-reduced version of AES, significantly weakening them. These findings are research advances and do not currently affect production systems.
details: Using Claude Mythos Preview, Anthropic researchers discovered improved attacks on cryptographic algorithms. These include significantly weakening HAWK, a post-quantum digital signature scheme, and identifying a new attack on round-reduced AES, the most widely used symmetric cipher. While substantial research advances, these do not currently affect any production systems.

HAWK is a third-round candidate for NIST's post-quantum cryptography standards, designed to resist quantum computers. Despite two years of expert review, Claude improved the best-known attack in just 60 hours, effectively halving its key strength.

The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is a symmetric cipher adopted by NIST in 2001 and is one of the most scrutinized algorithms. Claude found a way to break a weaker, round-reduced version, improving previous attack speeds by 200-800 times.

These results do not practically impact today’s computer systems as HAWK is not deployed and the AES attack is on a reduced version. Nevertheless, they demonstrate the potential for frontier AI models to uncover flaws in critical cryptographic algorithms, both pre- and post-deployment.

Claude Mythos Preview achieved these results mostly autonomously, with minimal human intervention. Each discovery cost approximately $100,000 in API costs, highlighting the resource intensity of such advanced AI cryptanalysis.
